definition: A tissue graft or tumor cell transplant derived from a species different from the recipient animal host.
etymology: From Ancient Greek ξένος (xénos, 'foreign, stranger') + graft.
manuscriptExample: Patient-derived xenograft (PDX) mouse models preserved the histological architecture and clonal diversity of primary tumors.
conferenceExample: The associate editor inquired whether in vivo antitumor efficacy was evaluated in orthotopic xenograft models.

definition: A chemical compound or drug that is foreign to a living organism or biological system.
manuscriptExample: Cytochrome P450 monooxygenases mediate the primary oxidative metabolism of foreign xenobiotics in hepatic tissue.
conferenceExample: We addressed Reviewer 1's questions regarding intracellular xenobiotic accumulation rates.
